## ✨ Added

- Optional web office (advanced, default off): set the "Web office suite" dropdown to `collabora`, `onlyoffice` or `euro-office`, fill in your document-server URL and a WOPI secret, and the wrapper turns on OpenCloud's built-in collaboration (WOPI) service and registers the editor.
- The document server itself (Collabora Online / CODE, OnlyOffice, or Euro Office, the sovereign OnlyOffice fork with image `ghcr.io/euro-office/documentserver`) runs as a separate container. See the README "Web office" section for the setup and reverse-proxy notes. A one-click Unraid template for the Euro Office document server is available in the junkerderprovinz feed.
- Euro Office is driven as the OnlyOffice product with the display name "Euro-Office" and WOPI proof-key verification disabled, matching OpenCloud's own euro-office example. OpenCloud makes it the default editor for the MS Office formats.

## ⚡ Improved

- Documented that the `posix` storage driver needs a Data volume on a filesystem with extended-attribute support (the Unraid array and cache/pool disks have it).
- Documented that for OnlyOffice and Euro Office the "Office WOPI secret" must equal the document server's JWT secret (`JWT_SECRET` / `EURO_OFFICE_JWT_SECRET`); for Collabora it is not required.

## 🐛 Fixed

- Files showed up but were greyed out and could not be opened or downloaded. The template shipped the storage driver blank, and OpenCloud reads a set-but-empty variable as an explicit override, which wiped its built-in `posix` default with an empty value. The template now sets `posix` explicitly. The unsupported `local` driver breaks the same way, so never use it. If your install already ran with a blank or `local` driver, set the driver to `posix` and start with a fresh Data folder, because the on-disk layout is fixed at first init.
- A fresh install crashed the gateway with "invalid IP-literal". The Public URL default used Unraid's [IP] and [PORT] tokens, which Unraid only substitutes in the WebUI field, not in environment variables, so OpenCloud received the literal text. The default is now a real editable placeholder, and the container falls back to its own IP if it is left unset, so it boots instead of crash-looping.
- A fresh install could hang during the one-time init. The init step opened an interactive prompt when it did not get a clear answer for the self-signed certificate; with no terminal that prompt spun forever. The container now always answers it non-interactively.
